newsitem.title: USA: Woolworth's closings hit workers, customers hard.
newsitem.headline: Woolworth's closings hit workers, customers hard.

text.p: Long-time employees of Woolworth's five-and-dime store on Chicago's State Street grew teary-eyed after they were told Thursday that their store and 400 others like it would be closed.
"It's so sad," said Dorine, a 20-year employee who has worked at five Woolworth's outlets, mostly at minimum wage, since she was 18.
"I just left a store they closed two years ago," she said from behind a food counter as hot dogs rotated inside a nearby cooker.
"It's almost like a family," she said, fighting back tears.

The two large though somewhat dingy Woolworth's outlets on the recently revitalized State Street have been crowded in by competitors, including newer-looking Walgreen's and Osco drugstores and a giant Toys 'R Us outlet.

The variety store, like many others in the 117-year-old chain, displayed caramel corn, coin banks and picnic coolers on one floor, with light bulbs, detergent, sewing materials and low-priced clothes on sale in the basement.

It was not clear what would happen to the stores' roughly 9,000 full- and part-time employees, although some of the stores could be converted into the company's successful boutique outlets such as Foot Locker.
Woolworth's said the closings will take several months.
Employees were told by managers not to comment.
"You know, to try to keep morale up," said an engineer named Joe.
"This is one of the larger stores, and we've been told the smaller stores might close first and they'd ship the merchandise here," he said. "We might be here a year from now, who knows?"
Customers were also saddened by the news.
"I heard it on the news this morning," said a woman leaving the store with a bag of sundries. "They must have a good reason for closing, but it's going to be an inconvenience to a lot of people."
Another woman shopper said she enjoyed shopping at Woolworth's for discounts on knick-knacks. "I like it around Christmastime. I can get bargains on little things, gifts."
